answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with a slashable identity bond: before voting, each agent locks collateral and registers one signed key. At the zenith of a dispute peers compare attestations; anyone caught vouching for clones at the summit of a fake coalition forfeits the whole bond. Because the kernel of the rule is capital, not key count, an attacker pays linearly for every extra identity, and one detected fraud destroys them all at once.
